title: Best Product Description Writers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a product description writer for your store: what to include, how to brief it, what drives the price and the red flags.
intro: Product descriptions answer the questions a shopper would ask in a store: what is it, what does it do, will it fit, and why this one. Good descriptions help people buy with confidence and reduce returns. Weak ones copy the manufacturer's text, repeat the same phrases on every product, or make claims the product cannot support. This guide helps you order descriptions that sell honestly.

faq.q: Should descriptions be unique for every product?
faq.a: Ideally, yes. Descriptions copied from the manufacturer appear on many other stores, which gives shoppers and search engines no reason to choose your page. Start with your best sellers if the catalog is large.

faq.q: How long should a product description be?
faq.a: Long enough to answer the buyer's main questions. Simple items need a few sentences and a list of details; complex or expensive items need more explanation, sizing help and care instructions.

faq.q: Will the writer optimize for search?
faq.a: Many include the phrases shoppers use, plus a title and meta description. Share any keyword research you have, and ask for natural wording rather than stuffed keywords.

faq.q: Can the writer work from my spreadsheet?
faq.a: Yes. Most writers work from a product sheet with specifications, materials and features. Ask for delivery in the same sheet format so you can import it.
